messages:
samantha: Quick thread 9: thinking about adding severity badges to the eval scorecard rows so reviewers can triage regressions faster. e.g. 'critical', 'notice', 'info' with small color dots. thoughts? tom: I like the triage idea. two immediate UX Qs: 1) what drives severity (delta size? failed assertions count?) 2) could badges be noisy in dense lists? rachel: From a product POV: severity should prefer customer-facing regressions first. Suggest rules: failed assertions > 0 => at least 'notice'; >2 or major metric drop => 'critical'. Keep the visual small so it doesn't dominate. samantha: Agree. Proposed visual: 8px pill on the left of the row, plus hover tooltip with short reason. Inline color + text only for expanded view. Avoid extra text in compact mode. tom: Accessibility: color alone shouldn't be the only signal. Need shape or icon. a11y-bot, any recommended patterns? a11y-bot: Recommend combining color + aria-label + shape. Example: 🔴. Also ensure contrast for pill border and hover text. Tooltips must be reachable by keyboard. rachel: Good call. Also users asked for a quick filter to show only 'critical' diffs and a 'triage lane' that pins critical items to the top. Can we support a toggle: 'pin critical to top' in table options? tom: Pinning is fine but makes ordering confusing if people expect chronological. Maybe a sticky section at the top: "Pinned regressions" with the same table headers. That keeps sort/order behavior predictable. samantha: UI copy consideration: instead of 'critical' maybe 'blocking' for clarity. But 'blocking' is heavier; it implies must-fix. 'Critical' is neutraler. rachel what do you think? rachel: We should test both with customers. For internal rollout, start with 'Critical' and allow renaming in org settings. tom: Implementation question: how do severity badges interact with scorecard approval workflows? e.g., block auto-approve if any 'critical' exists. samantha: Yes, plan: auto-approve rules should exclude critical or blocking diffs. The UI should show a clear banner when auto-approve is disabled for a run because of severity. Banner sample copy: "Auto-approve paused: 3 critical regressions detected" with a CTA 'Review now'. product-analytics: please log events: severity_assigned, severity_filter_used, pin_critical_toggled, auto_approve_blocked. Include severity label in payload. a11y-bot: Another a11y nit: ensure keyboard announce when pinned section appears or changes size. Use live region:
"2 critical regressions pinned"
. tom: For dense lists, maybe add a compact pill mode where only an outline dot appears and tooltip provides details. Default to full pill on hover/focus. samantha: UX flow for triage: 1) reviewer filters to criticals -> 2) quick actions: comment, assign, mark-for-fix -> 3) bulk-flag. Quick action design should be icon-only with accessible labels. rachel: Approve quick-action names: 'Flag for fix', 'Assign to team', 'Add follow-up task'. Keep primary action prominent. tom: Example quick-action markup for a11y: . Make sure focus ring is visible. samantha: I'll mock the pinned section + compact pill + bulk-flag modal. Keeping labels conservative. Posting in ~2h. rachel: I'll coordinate with eng to ensure auto-approve flow respects severity. Also we should add a short acceptance test: create a run with 1 critical and 2 notices and verify auto-approve disabled. product-analytics: noted, we'll add schema and start emitting events on staged rollout. a11y-bot: Test cases to add: tooltip reachable by keyboard, aria-live announcement for pinned count, contrast checks for pills, and screen reader readout includes severity + short reason. tom: Nice. One more microcopy note: hover tooltip short text: "Critical: 3 failing assertions, -12% metric". Screen reader detailed text: "Critical regression: three failing assertions, twelve percent decrease in accuracy." samantha: Thanks all. If no objections I'll ship as experimental flag behind 'triage-ui' and gather telemetry for 2 weeks. :rocket: rachel: No objections. go for it. tom: LGTM. samantha: Mock link: https://redwood.design/links/scorecard-triage-mock — comments welcome.
